title: C-Side Step 3 / R-Side v1.3 System Synthesis

executive_conclusion.reason: The existing 5-seed x 4-topology long-horizon benchmark already uses the final recommended C-side checkpoint (r_feasibility_safe_last.pt).

step3_interpretation.overload_aware: Mixed-stress validation removes its brittleness (7.46% -> 0.00%), but it still does not beat r_feasibility_safe.
step3_interpretation.r_feasibility_safe: Remains the safest default; its 1.13% best-checkpoint heavy blocking in Step 3 is seed-variance, and its last checkpoint stays at 0%.

final_c_side_decision.conservative_fallback: Use the last checkpoint when training budget allows; it is consistently 0% across standard/medium/heavy stress.

code_status.recommended_code_change: Change argparse defaults to validation_stress_levels='standard,medium,heavy' and checkpoint_metric='max_blocking'.

failure_mode_interpretation.why_v13_wins_cost239: Small topology; learned ranker finds path/block combinations that reduce server overload.
failure_mode_interpretation.why_v13_wins_jpn48: Large physical network offers many candidates; ranker scoring over 48 candidates outperforms greedy hop-ordered first-fit.
failure_mode_interpretation.why_german17_neutral: KSP-FF already near-optimal for this node layout and load.
failure_mode_interpretation.why_nsfnet_weak: Compute saturation dominates at ~15% blocking; R-side path optimization has limited headroom.
failure_mode_interpretation.future_gain_direction: Better C-side allocation or joint C-R selection, not merely larger R-side candidate sets.

optional_smoke_test_if_equivalence_must_.description: Compare original r_feasibility_safe_last.pt against step3_mixedstress_20260704_last.pt on COST239 with v1.3.

code: Change train_agent_c_with_frozen_r.py defaults: --validation_stress_levels standard,medium,heavy and --checkpoint_metric max_blocking
Verify backward compatibility when --validation_stress_levels is empty
science: Investigate joint C-R optimization conditioned on anticipated server load
Evaluate per-topology C training under the same r_feasibility_safe representation
Longer training run for overload_aware with mixed-stress validation to strengthen the negative result
avoid: Adding more hand-crafted C-side features before ruling out checkpoint-selection issues
Increasing R-side candidate set beyond 48 without evidence that no_suitable_block is limiting
Claiming v1.3 superiority on all topologies

paper_ready_phrases.c_side: The overload_aware feature set did not provide a systematic reduction in server-overload blocking compared with r_feasibility_safe. The critical C-side improvement is the validation regime, not another hand-crafted feature set.
paper_ready_phrases.r_side: With C-side fixed to the stable r_feasibility_safe checkpoint, the v1.3 hybrid significantly reduces blocking on COST239 (-25.9%, p=0.0011) and JPN48 (-12.6%, p=0.0067), is neutral on German17 (+0.5%, p=0.77), and shows only a small non-significant trend on NSFNET (-2.4%, p=0.37).
paper_ready_phrases.failure_mode: Across all topologies residual blocking is dominated by server overload, so future gains likely require improved compute-side allocation or joint routing-and-offloading decisions rather than larger routing candidate sets alone.
paper_ready_phrases.one_line_takeaway: The practical advance on the C side is a stress-robust validation regime; the practical advance on the R side is a learned ranker that improves blocking on two of four topologies when the C-side policy is already stable.
